# Glossary {#sec-glossary .unnumbered}

This appendix collects, in one alphabetical list, the concepts
defined in each chapter's 'vocabulary of this chapter' section
together with the commands, functions, tools, and services the
book relies on. The per-chapter vocabulary sections remain in
place; this is a second view of them and not a replacement.

Each entry names the chapter that introduces or develops it, and
a term developed in more than one chapter names each. Entries
are alphabetized by the term itself, so a function is filed
under its own name rather than under the package that supplies
it: look for `tar_make()` under T and `renv::restore()` under R.

## A {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-apptainer-build}**`apptainer build`.** Converts an OCI image into a single SIF
file that runs without root, which is what makes it acceptable
on a shared cluster and depositable as an archival artifact.
(@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-apptainer}**Apptainer (formerly Singularity).** A container runtime built
for shared high-performance computing, where users are not
administrators. Its SIF format is a single checksummable file.
(@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-archetype}**Archetype.** The kind of research object a compendium is (data
analysis, manuscript, package, simulation study, or blog), which
varies the layout and the gates but not the underlying
machinery. (@sec-compendium)


## B {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-backend}**Backend.** The mechanism that supplies the environment. Docker
is the container backend; Nix is a container-free backend that
declares the environment directly. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-base-image}**Base image.** The starting image a recipe builds on, named on
the `FROM` line. Here, a Rocker image providing a fixed R
version on a fixed operating system. (@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-baseline-test}**Baseline test.** A test, in a file named `test-baseline-*.R`,
that recomputes key outputs and compares them with values
recorded in an earlier session and committed, using
`expect_equal()` with a stated tolerance. It is the evidence L3
requires. (@sec-testing, @sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-binder}**Binder.** A service that builds an environment from a public
repository and serves it in a browser, so a reviewer can run an
analysis with nothing installed locally. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-branch}**Branch.** A movable name for a line of development. The
default branch is conventionally called `main`.
(@sec-version-control)


## C {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-capture}**Capture.** Fixing an input so that it cannot drift: writing a
lockfile, building a container image. Capture sets the
reproducibility level. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-checksum}**Checksum.** A short fingerprint, computed from a file's or an
object's bytes by a hash function such as SHA-256, with the
property that any change to the input, however small, changes
the fingerprint. A stored checksum lets a later run detect that
an input has been altered. (@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-code-chunk}**Code chunk.** A block of executable code embedded in a
literate document, delimited from the prose, whose output is
inserted into the rendered document at the chunk's position.
(@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-codecheck}**CODECHECK.** A scheme in which an independent person re-runs a
submitted analysis and certifies the result, catching the class
of failure where the author's own checks encode the author's own
assumptions. (@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-codespaces-and-devcontainers}**Codespaces and devcontainers.** A specification, and a hosted
implementation of it, for describing the development environment
an editor should open a project inside. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-commit}**Commit.** A recorded snapshot of the tracked files at one
moment, carrying an author, a timestamp, a message, and an
immutable identifier (a *hash*). The atomic unit of history.
(@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-computational-reproducibility}**Computational reproducibility.** Obtaining the same numerical
results from the same data and the same code, on another machine
or at a later time. (@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-conda-and-pixi}**conda and pixi.** Cross-language environment managers that pin
R and Python packages without a container. `pixi` is the option
that reproduces natively on Windows. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-container}**Container.** A running instance of an image. One image can
start many containers; each begins from the same frozen
filesystem. (@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-container-image}**Container image.** A packaged environment, built from a
recipe, that carries the operating system, the system libraries,
and the language runtime, and runs identically wherever a
container runtime runs. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-controlled-access}**Controlled access.** A deposit arrangement in which a
repository holds restricted data behind an approval process,
rather than releasing it on request, so that a data-use
agreement and the terms a participant consented to are
honored while the record stays discoverable and citable.
(@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-continuous-integration}**Continuous integration (CI).** A hosted service that, on every
committed change to a repository, checks out the code onto a
fresh virtual machine, rebuilds the project, and runs a defined
set of checks, reporting success or failure automatically.
(@sec-verification)


## D {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-daemon}**Daemon.** A background system service that runs continuously
with elevated privilege. Docker relies on one; Podman and
Apptainer do not, which is why they run without administrative
rights. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-data-availability-statement}**Data-availability statement.** A sentence in a manuscript,
or in its compendium, naming where the data behind its
results can be obtained: an open deposit's DOI, the name and
access route of a controlled-access repository, or the
terms under which the data cannot be shared at all.
(@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-data-validation-test}**Data-validation test.** A check on the data itself rather than
the code: that a value lies in a plausible range, that no
impossible ages appear, that the expected columns are present.
(@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-dated-snapshot}**Dated snapshot.** A view of a repository frozen as it stood on
a particular calendar day, so that an install run today and one
run next year fetch the same versions. (@sec-dependencies,
@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-dependency-graph}**Dependency graph.** The graph whose nodes are the steps and
whose edges record that one step consumes what another produces.
A valid pipeline's graph is a *directed acyclic graph* (DAG):
directed because inputs flow to outputs, and acyclic because a
step cannot, directly or transitively, depend on its own output.
(@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-dependency-manifest-gate}**Dependency-manifest gate.** A CI check that enforces the
dependency invariant of @sec-dependencies. In its strict,
R-package form it requires every package the code uses to be
declared in `DESCRIPTION` and pinned in `renv.lock`. For a
research compendium, whose `DESCRIPTION` declares only the API
exported from `R/` while analysis scripts legitimately draw on
packages present in `renv.lock` but not in `DESCRIPTION`, it
enforces the weaker inclusion that every package the code uses
is pinned in `renv.lock`. (@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-description}**`DESCRIPTION`.** The human-authored file that declares a
project's direct dependencies by role (`Imports`, `Suggests`,
`Depends`), with optional version floors. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-determinant-stack}**Determinant stack.** The layered set of things a computational
result depends upon, from the hardware at the base through the
environment and the packages to the analysis code and the data
at the top. A layer is 'pinned' when it has been fixed to a
recorded value. (@sec-crisis, @sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-determinism}**Determinism (of a render).** The property that rendering the
same source under the same environment produces a byte-for-byte
identical output file. A rendered PDF is usually not
deterministic in this strict sense, for reasons developed below.
(@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-digest}**`digest()`.** Computes a content hash of an R object. Used to
verify that a regenerated computational output matches a
recorded one, on objects rather than on rendered documents.
(@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-docker}**Docker.** The most widely used container platform, and one
instrument for reaching a pinned environment rather than a
synonym for reproducibility. (@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-docker-build-and-docker-run}**`docker build` and `docker run`.** Build an image from a
recipe and start a container from an image. The image is
durable; the container is ephemeral. (@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-docker-hub-and-ghcr}**Docker Hub and GHCR.** Container registries. A pushed image is
a cache and not the record: the committed recipe is the record,
because a registry can delete, rate-limit, or repoint what it
holds. (@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-docker-pull-and-docker-inspect}**`docker pull` and `docker inspect`.** Fetch an image and read
its metadata, including the content digest that a reproducible
recipe pins instead of a tag. (@sec-containers)


## E {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-expectation}**Expectation.** A single assertion, such as
`expect_equal(actual, expected)`, that passes or fails.
(@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-expect-equal-and-the-other-expectations}**`expect_equal()` and the other expectations.** The assertions
of `tinytest`. A file of bare, top-level expectation calls is a
complete test file, and `expect_inherits()`, `expect_true()`,
and `expect_error()` cover most of the rest. (@sec-testing)


## F {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-fair}**FAIR.** A set of principles holding that a research object
should be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable,
formulated for data and later adapted for research software.
(@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-forge}**Forge.** A platform that hosts a version-controlled repository
and runs its continuous integration. GitHub and GitLab are the
two principal forges; GitLab is frequently self-hosted by
universities. (@sec-verification, @sec-archiving)


## G {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-git-add}**`git add`.** Stages changes for the next commit. Staging is
what lets a commit be one idea rather than a snapshot of
whatever is on disk. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-clone-push-pull-fetch}**`git clone`, `push`, `pull`, `fetch`.** Move history between a
local repository and a remote. A remote serves backup,
distribution, and collaboration, which are three purposes worth
keeping separate. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-commit}**`git commit`.** Records the staged changes with a message and
an immutable identifier. The atomic unit of the history.
(@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-diff}**`git diff`.** Shows what changed, between the working tree and
the index, or between any two commits. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-filter-repo}**`git filter-repo`.** Rewrites history to remove content,
producing new hashes for every commit from the offending one
forward. The tool of last resort after protected data has been
committed, and no substitute for notifying whoever is
responsible for the data. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-init}**`git init`.** Creates a repository in a directory. The
`.gitignore` should be written before the first commit, not
after. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-log-and-git-show}**`git log` and `git show`.** Read the history: `log` lists
commits, `show` prints one commit's message and its diff
together. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-switch-and-git-merge}**`git switch` and `git merge`.** Move between branches and
rejoin them. A merge commit is the only commit with two parents,
which is what records that two lines of work came back together.
(@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-git-tag}**`git tag`.** Marks a particular commit permanently, such as
the state of an analysis at submission. Cheap to place and
expensive to omit. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-github-actions}**GitHub Actions.** GitHub's continuous-integration service,
configured by YAML workflow files under `.github/workflows/`.
(@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-github-and-gitlab}**GitHub and GitLab.** The two principal forges. GitLab is
frequently self-hosted by institutions that forbid pushing to a
public forge, and a compendium's reproducibility machinery
should be portable between them. (@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-gitignore}**`.gitignore`.** A file listing path patterns that git should
not track, used to keep derived outputs, large data, and,
critically, sensitive files out of the history.
(@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-groundhog-library}**`groundhog.library()`.** Loads a package as it stood on a
given date, a lighter alternative to a lockfile that
reconstructs by date rather than by record. (@sec-dependencies)


## I {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-image}**Image.** A frozen, read-only filesystem together with
metadata, bundling an operating system, R, a set of packages,
and configuration. It is analogous to a snapshot of a fully
installed computer, packaged so it can be shipped.
(@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-input-addressed}**Input-addressed.** Identified by a hash of the build inputs
rather than by a mutable name, so that a reference cannot
silently point at different content later. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-install-packages}**`install.packages()`.** Base R's installer. Pointed at a live
repository it resolves 'the current version' to whatever is
current on the day it runs, which is why a reproducible recipe
points it at a dated snapshot or replaces it with a lockfile
restore. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-integration-test}**Integration test.** A check that several components behave
correctly when composed into a pipeline, from raw input to final
result. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-invalidation}**Invalidation.** The act of marking a target out of date
because something it depends on, a file, an upstream target, a
function, or a package, has changed. (@sec-pipelines)


## K {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-knitr-and-sweave}**`knitr` and Sweave.** The engines that execute code inside a
literate document. Sweave came first; `knitr` superseded it and
underlies both R Markdown and Quarto's R support.
(@sec-literate)


## L {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-landmine}**Landmine.** A pattern in a document that makes the render
succeed for its author and fail for a later reader, by reaching
outside the captured and committed material. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-latex-and-tinytex}**LaTeX and TinyTeX.** The typesetting system a PDF render
requires, and a small R-managed distribution of it. Belongs in
the image rather than assumed on the host. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-layer}**Layer.** Each instruction in an image's recipe produces one
filesystem layer. An image is the stack of its layers, and
identical layers are shared and cached across images.
(@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-library-and-require}**`library()` and `require()`.** The two calls that attach a
package to the current session. Both are scanned when a
dependency check derives what the code uses, so a package loaded
this way must be declared and pinned. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-linting}**Linting.** Static analysis of source code for stylistic and
likely-error patterns, performed by `lintr`, without running the
code. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-lintr-and-styler}**`lintr` and `styler`.** Static analysis and automatic
reformatting for R source. Legibility is a validation feature:
code nobody can read is code nobody can check. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-literate-programming}**Literate programming.** Writing narrative prose and executable
code together in one source document, so the document is at once
the program and its explanation. The term is Knuth's.
(@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-lockfile}**Lockfile.** A machine-generated file, `renv.lock`, recording
the R version, the package repositories, and the exact version
and source of every package the project uses, with metadata
copied from each package's `DESCRIPTION`. (@sec-levels,
@sec-dependencies)


## M {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-make}**`make`.** Rebuilds targets whose modification time is older
than a prerequisite's. Conservative in one direction and
unreliable in the other: it will rebuild what did not need it,
and miss a change that leaves timestamps untouched.
(@sec-pipelines)


## N {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-nix-and-guix}**Nix and Guix.** Declarative package managers that pin an
entire dependency graph, from the system libraries upward, to a
single revision. They reach a pinned environment from a recipe
rather than from a built artifact. (@sec-backends)


## O {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-oci-image}**OCI image.** An image built to the Open Container Initiative
specification, the common format that Docker, Podman, and
Apptainer can all consume. A Docker image is an OCI image.
(@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-oci-tarball-or-sif-file}**OCI tarball or SIF file.** A container image exported as a
single file, checksummable and depositable as an archival
artifact. An OCI image is exported as a tar archive, whereas SIF
is the self-contained single-file format used by the Apptainer
runtime. (@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-oracle}**Oracle.** The source of independent truth a test compares
against; the known correct answer. (@sec-testing)


## P {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-package-churn}**Package churn (code rot).** The gradual breakage of
once-working code as the packages beneath it are updated over
time. (@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-package-library}**Package library.** The directory into which R installs
packages. A project-local library belongs to one project rather
than being shared across all of a user's work.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-package-record}**Package record.** The `renv.lock` entry for one package: its
name, exact version, and source, plus fields such as `Imports`
and `License` copied from its `DESCRIPTION`. It contains no
checksum of the package's files; the `Hash` field written by
`renv` before 1.1.0 was a fingerprint of `DESCRIPTION` fields
used to key the package cache. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-package-repository}**Package repository.** A server, such as CRAN or the Posit
Package Manager, from which packages are installed.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-pacman-p-load}**`pacman::p_load()`.** Loads packages and installs any that are
missing. Convenient and a landmine in a sealed document: it
reaches the network at render time and pins nothing.
(@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-pandoc}**pandoc.** The document converter a render invokes after the
code has run, turning the executed markdown into the requested
output format. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-persistent-identifier}**Persistent identifier (DOI).** A durable, resolvable name for
a deposited artifact, such as a Digital Object Identifier, that
continues to resolve even if the artifact moves.
(@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-pipeline}**Pipeline.** An analysis expressed as a set of steps, each
declaring its inputs and outputs, so that the whole can be
re-executed by a single command that runs the steps in
dependency order. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-pkg-fun}**`pkg::fun()`.** A namespaced call, which uses a function
without attaching its package. It still creates a dependency,
and a scanner that looked only for `library()` would miss it.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-podman}**Podman.** A daemonless, rootless container runtime that runs
the same images as Docker. The usual answer where Docker Desktop
licensing is a constraint. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-podman-run}**`podman run`.** Starts a container without a root daemon,
consuming the same image format Docker produces. Swapping the
runtime changes the launcher and not the reproducibility level.
(@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-posit-package-manager}**Posit Package Manager.** A package repository that serves
dated snapshots and prebuilt binaries, so that an install run
today and one run next year fetch the same versions.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-precommit}**`precommit`.** Runs checks before a commit is recorded,
keeping trivia out of the history. It can be skipped, which is
why it complements rather than replaces continuous integration.
(@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-pre-commit-hook}**Pre-commit hook.** A script that git runs automatically before
a commit is recorded, used here to run the linter and the styler
as a gate. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-prerequisite}**Prerequisite.** In Make, an input a target depends on. If any
prerequisite is newer than the target, the target is out of
date. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-profile}**Profile.** The base-image bundle a project is built from, such
as `minimal`, `tidyverse`, `rstudio`, or `publishing`. It
selects the `FROM` image. (@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-progressive-disclosure}**Progressive disclosure.** The property that one layout
supports a project's evolution from one archetype to another
with no reorganization. (@sec-compendium)

[]{#gloss-pull-request}**Pull request (merge request).** A proposal, made on the
remote, to merge one branch or fork into another, reviewed
before it is accepted. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-purely-functional-package-manager}**Purely functional package manager.** A package manager, such
as Nix, in which the installed result is a deterministic
function of the declared inputs, so that the same declaration
yields a deterministic, reproducible environment.
(@sec-backends)


## Q {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-quarto-and-r-markdown}**Quarto and R Markdown.** The literate-document systems this
book uses: prose and executable code in one source, rendered to
HTML, PDF, and other formats. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-quarto-render}**`quarto render`.** Executes a document's code and produces its
output formats. With `freeze` configured it may replay a cache
instead of executing, which is why a gate that must exercise the
code has to clear the cache first. (@sec-literate)


## R {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-r-cmd-check}**`R CMD check`.** The standard R command that builds a package,
runs its tests, and applies dozens of standardized checks; here
it serves as an integrity gate on the compendium's package skin
(`R/`, the tests, `DESCRIPTION`). It does not check `analysis/`,
which `.Rbuildignore` excludes from the build.
(@sec-compendium, @sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-rang-groundhog-and-capsule}**`rang`, `groundhog`, and `capsule`.** Lighter alternatives to
a lockfile that reconstruct a package set from a date. Useful
when no lockfile survives, and an approximation rather than a
record. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-raw-versus-derived-data}**Raw versus derived data.** Immutable original inputs versus
the processed datasets regenerated from them by code.
(@sec-compendium)

[]{#gloss-recipe}**Recipe (or command).** The shell command Make runs to bring a
target up to date from its prerequisites. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-registry}**Registry.** A server that stores and distributes container
images, from which collaborators pull a pre-built environment.
GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) and Docker Hub are the two in
common use. (@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-remote}**Remote.** A copy of the repository hosted elsewhere, typically
on GitHub or GitLab, used for backup, distribution, and
collaboration. `origin` is the conventional name of the primary
remote. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-remotes-install-github}**`remotes::install_github()`.** Installs a package from a git
repository rather than a package repository. Reproducible only
if pinned to a commit or a tag. (@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-render-gate}**Render gate.** A CI check that re-renders the compendium's
report (an R Markdown or Quarto document) from source and fails
the build if the render errors. (@sec-compendium,
@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-render}**Render (verb and noun).** To execute a literate source
document and produce a finished output file (HTML, PDF, Word);
and the resulting file itself. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-rendering-toolchain}**Rendering toolchain.** The programs a render invokes behind
the scenes: `knitr` or the Quarto engine to run the code,
`pandoc` to convert the result, and, for PDF, a LaTeX
distribution to typeset it. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-renv-and-packrat}**`renv` and `packrat`.** The current and superseded R
dependency managers. Both pair a project-local library with a
lockfile; `renv` rebuilt the interface around a small set of
verbs and a shared cache. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-renv-init}**`renv::init()`.** Creates a project-local library and
lockfile, taking a project from unpinned to pinned packages.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-renv-restore}**`renv::restore()`.** Reads the lockfile and installs the
recorded versions into the library. The command a collaborator
runs on a fresh clone. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-renv-snapshot}**`renv::snapshot()`.** Reads the library and writes what it
finds into the lockfile. Snapshot writes; restore reads.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-renv-status}**`renv::status()`.** Reports disagreement between the library
and the lockfile, and is the first diagnostic when a restore
appears not to have worked. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-replicability}**Replicability.** Obtaining consistent findings from a new
study, with new data, aimed at the same question. (@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-repository}**Repository (repo).** A directory whose contents and full
history git tracks, held in a hidden `.git` subdirectory. A
*clone* is a complete copy of a repository, history and all.
(@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-reproduced}**Reproduced.** Obtaining the same computational result by
re-executing the same code on the same data. Contrast
**replicated**, obtaining a consistent finding from a new study
with new data. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-reproducibility-test}**Reproducibility test.** A check that a recorded computational
result regenerates. The form that can fail is the baseline test;
two runs in one session do not qualify. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-research-compendium}**Research compendium.** A single self-describing directory
bundling the code, data, prose, and environment record of an
analysis, organized by convention so that it can be located and
re-run. (@sec-crisis, @sec-compendium)

[]{#gloss-restore}**Restore.** The reverse act of reading the lockfile and
reinstalling exactly the packages it records.
(@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-rix-rix}**`rix::rix()`.** Generates a `default.nix` pinning an R
version, a package set, and the `nixpkgs` revision that
determines everything beneath them. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-rng-kind}**RNG kind.** The random-number algorithm in force, set by
`RNGkind()`. Two runs with the same seed but a different kind
draw different numbers. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-rngkind}**`RNGkind()`.** Selects the random-number generator algorithm.
Its `sample.kind` default changed in R 3.6.0, so the same seed
draws different numbers under different R versions unless the
kind is recorded. (@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-robustness}**Robustness.** Reaching the same qualitative conclusion from
the same data under different but defensible analytical choices.
(@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-rocker}**Rocker.** The community project that publishes the standard R
Docker images. (@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-rootless}**Rootless.** Able to run under an ordinary user account,
without the `root` superuser privilege. A requirement on shared
clusters, where users are not administrators. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-r-package-skin}**R-package skin.** The minimal set of files (`DESCRIPTION`,
`NAMESPACE`, an `R/` directory) that makes a directory a valid R
package, and therefore checkable by the R build tools.
(@sec-compendium)

[]{#gloss-runner}**Runner.** The fresh, ephemeral machine (usually a virtual
machine or a container) on which the CI service executes the
workflow. It is discarded after the run, so nothing persists
between runs except what the workflow explicitly restores.
(@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-runtime}**Runtime.** The program that runs a container image: Docker,
Podman, or Apptainer. The runtime is interchangeable when the
image is a standard OCI image. (@sec-backends)


## S {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-saverds-and-readrds}**`saveRDS()` and `readRDS()`.** Write and read a single R
object to a file. The ordinary way to record the baseline that a
reproducibility test compares against. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-sealed-render}**Sealed render.** A document in which every reported number and
figure is regenerated from the code that produces it on each
build, so the prose cannot drift from the analysis.
(@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-seed-and-rng-kind}**Seed and RNG kind.** The seed (`set.seed`) is the fixed
starting point that makes a random draw repeatable; the RNG kind
is the generator algorithm that turns that seed into numbers,
and its default has changed across R versions. (@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-sessioninfo}**`sessionInfo()`.** Reports the R version, platform, and
attached packages of the current session. A record of what ran,
not a mechanism for making it run again. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-set-seed}**`set.seed()`.** Fixes the starting point of the random-number
stream so that a stochastic result repeats. Necessary but not
sufficient: the generator algorithm must be fixed as well.
(@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-sif}**SIF.** The Singularity Image Format, a single-file archive
that Apptainer produces from an image, suitable for depositing
alongside a compendium. (@sec-backends)

[]{#gloss-silent-default}**Silent default.** A behavior that software applies unless told
otherwise, and that can change between software versions without
any error or warning to the analyst. (@sec-crisis)

[]{#gloss-snakemake-and-nextflow}**Snakemake and Nextflow.** Pipeline tools from the
bioinformatics community, language-agnostic and built for
cluster execution. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-snapshot}**Snapshot.** The act of scanning a project, resolving the
versions currently installed, and writing them into the
lockfile. (@sec-dependencies)

[]{#gloss-source-date-epoch}**`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.** A conventional environment variable,
honored by many document tools, that fixes the timestamp a build
embeds, so that two builds do not differ merely because they ran
at different moments. (@sec-literate)

[]{#gloss-staging-area}**Staging area (index).** The set of changes marked, with `git
add`, to go into the next commit. Staging lets a commit hold a
chosen subset of the current changes. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-staleness}**Staleness (out-of-date).** The condition of a target whose
inputs have changed since it was last built, so that its stored
output no longer reflects its inputs. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-styling}**Styling.** Automatic reformatting of source code to a
consistent layout, performed by `styler`. (@sec-testing)


## T {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-tag}**Tag.** A permanent, human-readable name for one specific
commit, used to mark a milestone such as a manuscript
submission. (@sec-version-control)

[]{#gloss-tag-and-digest}**Tag and digest.** A tag, such as `rocker/tidyverse:4.4.0`, is
a human-readable pointer that may later be repointed. A digest,
`@sha256:...`, is an immutable hash of the image's exact
content. The same digest always denotes byte-identical bytes.
(@sec-containers)

[]{#gloss-target}**Target.** A single step in the pipeline, together with the
output it produces. The word is shared by Make and `targets`,
with a shift of emphasis: for Make a target is a file, for
`targets` it is more often an R object. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-targets}**`targets`.** A function-oriented pipeline tool for R that
hashes function bodies and R objects rather than file
timestamps, so it detects changes a Makefile can miss.
(@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-tar-make}**`tar_make()`.** Runs a `targets` pipeline, rebuilding only the
targets that are out of date and everything downstream of them.
(@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-tar-outdated}**`tar_outdated()`.** Reports which targets `tar_make()` would
rebuild, without rebuilding them. The way to check a prediction
about the dependency graph before paying for it.
(@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-tar-target}**`tar_target()`.** Declares one node of a `targets` pipeline: a
name, the expression that computes it, and optionally a format
such as `file`. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-tar-visnetwork}**`tar_visnetwork()`.** Draws the pipeline's dependency graph,
derived from the code rather than from a hand-maintained
declaration. (@sec-pipelines)

[]{#gloss-the-five-pillars}**The Five Pillars.** The five artifacts a compendium manages,
one per capture point: the `Dockerfile`, `renv.lock`,
`.Rprofile`, the source code, and the data. (@sec-compendium)

[]{#gloss-the-level-ladder}**The level ladder (L0 to L3).** The four-rung scale, L0
locatable, L1 pinned packages, L2 pinned environment, L3
verified, used throughout this book to grade how far down the
stack an analysis has been secured. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-tinytest}**`tinytest`.** A lightweight, zero-dependency R testing
framework in which a test file is a plain script of bare,
top-level expectation calls [@vanderloo2020]. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-tinytest-and-testthat}**`tinytest` and `testthat`.** R testing frameworks. `tinytest`
has no dependencies and its test files are plain scripts of bare
expectations, which is why this book uses it. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-two-layer-team-model}**Two-layer team model.** A division of a project into a
slow-moving environment layer, fixed once by a team lead, and a
fast-moving package layer, extended by every contributor.
(@sec-archiving)


## U {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-union-model}**Union model.** The rule that the project lockfile records the
union of every package any contributor has installed, so that a
rebuilt image carries what the whole team needs, not only what
one member used. (@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-unit-test}**Unit test.** A focused check that one small piece of code,
typically a single function, behaves as intended on known
inputs. (@sec-testing)

[]{#gloss-up-to-date}**Up-to-date (skippable).** The condition of a target whose
inputs have not changed since it was last built, so that
rebuilding it would reproduce the stored output and can be
skipped. (@sec-pipelines)


## V {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-validation}**Validation.** Confirming that the captured inputs actually
suffice, by rebuilding and re-running. Validation does not pin
anything new; it checks. (@sec-levels)

[]{#gloss-verification}**Verification.** Rebuilding the compendium's environment from
its recipe, re-running the analysis in it, and comparing the
regenerated outputs with a committed baseline, within a stated
tolerance, by means of a baseline test; passing it is what the
ladder calls level L3. (@sec-verification)


## W {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-workflow}**Workflow.** The file, written in YAML, that tells the CI
service what to do: which events trigger it, what environment to
run in, and what commands to execute. On GitHub these files live
under `.github/workflows/`; on GitLab the single file is
`.gitlab-ci.yml`. (@sec-verification)

[]{#gloss-working-tree}**Working tree.** The ordinary files in the repository directory
as they currently exist on disk, as opposed to the versions
recorded in the history. (@sec-version-control)


## Z {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[]{#gloss-zenodo}**Zenodo.** A general-purpose research repository, operated at
CERN, that mints a DOI for any deposited file set.
(@sec-archiving)

[]{#gloss-zzcollab}**zzcollab.** The framework this book uses to compose the
reproducibility tools into one system, organized around the
levels ladder. (@sec-compendium)

[]{#gloss-zzrenvcheck-check-packages}**`zzrenvcheck::check_packages()`.** Checks the dependency triad
and can repair it, writing a missing package into `DESCRIPTION`
and injecting a resolved entry into the lockfile.
(@sec-dependencies)
